findings.highlight: our barely budding relationship is now on the brink of collapse
findings.evidenceJa: けれど、その時深刻な話をしなかったせいで、始まったばかりの関係が、あっさりと破局を迎えた。
findings.explanation: Haruki says that because he and Mari failed to have the serious talk, their newly begun relationship readily reached a breakup. The English leaves them only on the brink of collapse, withholding the completed rupture that defines the route's present state.
findings.japanese:
けれど、その時深刻な話をしなかったせいで、
始まったばかりの関係が、あっさりと破局を迎えた。
findings.todokanai: Even so, it's exactly because we didn't manage to have that serious talk that our barely budding relationship is now on the brink of collapse.

findings.highlight: I'm alright with whatever time you decide.
findings.evidenceJa: 「いつならＯＫなんだよ？もうすぐ３月だぞ？」
findings.explanation: Takeya asks Haruki when Haruki will be available, pressing him to commit to a date before March. The English instead has Takeya offer unrestricted availability, reversing who must answer the scheduling question.
findings.japanese:
「いつならＯＫなんだよ？
もうすぐ３月だぞ？」
findings.todokanai: "I'm alright with whatever time you decide. It's almost March, you know?"

findings.highlight: they only work on the last days before the deadline, so nobody has come
findings.evidenceJa: …さすがに奴らは締め切り明けの日曜なんで、誰も来てないが
findings.explanation: The office is empty because this is the Sunday after the deadline, when the exhausted staff are finally absent. The English says they work only immediately before deadlines, losing the post-deadline timing and the workplace joke.
findings.japanese:
「で、今からこっちに顔出すか？　俺はいるぞ。
…さすがに奴らは締め切り明けの日曜なんで、
誰も来てないが」
findings.todokanai: "So are you going to show up here? I'm here. …As you'd expect, they only work on the last days before the deadline, so nobody has come."

findings.highlight: the memory of a certain someone inevitably popped into my mind
findings.evidenceJa: それでもなんとか無事故で切り抜けて、だから、いつかの誰かを思い出さずには済んだ。
findings.explanation: Because Haruki gets through the drive without an accident, he is spared having to remember a certain earlier driver. The English says the safe arrival inevitably makes him remember her, exactly reversing the negated result; the next line then jokes that articulating this has made him remember after all.
findings.japanese:
それでもなんとか無事故で切り抜けて、
だから、いつかの誰かを思い出さずには済んだ。
findings.todokanai: With the way we ended up reaching our venue without accident, the memory of a certain someone inevitably popped into my mind.

findings.highlight: "I see you still have that rigid way of thinking, huh, Haruki?"
findings.evidenceJa: 「相変わらず春希らしい堅実な考え方だねぇ」
findings.explanation: Takeya's career choice is called prudent or steady; the English calls it rigid.
findings.japanese: 「相変わらず春希らしい堅実な考え方だねぇ」
findings.todokanai: "I see you still have that rigid way of thinking, huh, Haruki?"

findings.highlight: I guess I just think I should still be working.
findings.evidenceJa: 一応、セミナーにはもう何度か参加してるけど、イマイチピンとこないって言うか…まだ働くんだっていう実感がね～
findings.explanation: Io has attended several recruiting seminars but still cannot quite feel that she is actually about to enter the workforce. The English says she thinks she should still be working, producing the wrong career state and an incoherent reply.
findings.japanese:
「一応、セミナーにはもう何度か参加してるけど、
イマイチピンとこないって言うか…
まだ働くんだっていう実感がね～」
findings.todokanai: "I attend seminars every now and then, but maybe I think it doesn't really help me or… I guess I just think I should still be working."

findings.highlight: Up until the point where he has to help a client, that is.
findings.evidenceJa: 「顧客に手を出したことが発覚するまではね」
findings.explanation: Io jokes that Takeya will prosper in insurance only until it is discovered that he has made a pass at or slept with a client. 手を出す is the punch line; the English turns the misconduct into the ordinary act of helping a client.
findings.japanese: 「顧客に手を出したことが発覚するまではね」
findings.todokanai: "Up until the point where he has to help a client, that is."

findings.highlight: "Before this, when I called him, he started babbling on in Kansai dialect."
findings.evidenceJa:
「この前電話かかってきたとき、
いきなり関西弁でまくしたてられてさ…」
findings.explanation: Hayasaka called Haruki to ask for Setsuna's contact details; the English suggests Haruki called Hayasaka.
findings.japanese:
「この前電話かかってきたとき、
いきなり関西弁でまくしたてられてさ…」
findings.todokanai: "Before this, when I called him, he started babbling on in Kansai dialect."

findings.highlight: Katou-san and I weren't even in the same class. We were farthest apart on attendance numbers
findings.evidenceJa: 「わたし、加藤さんとは同じクラスどころか、出席番号も一番違いだったのに…」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says that she and Tomo were not merely in the same class: their attendance numbers were one apart. The English reverses both facts, putting them in different classes and at opposite ends of the roll.
findings.japanese:
「わたし、加藤さんとは同じクラスどころか、
出席番号も一番違いだったのに…」
findings.todokanai: "Katou-san and I weren't even in the same class. We were farthest apart on attendance numbers…"

findings.highlight: So I guess you could say it's not your fault.
findings.evidenceJa: …だから難攻不落だったとも言えるが
findings.explanation: Takeya says Setsuna's lifelong obliviousness to romance is precisely why she was an impregnable fortress. The English replaces the comic explanation for her legendary unattainability with generic reassurance that it was not her fault.
findings.japanese:
「ま、雪菜ちゃん、
昔っからそういうこと疎かったもんなぁ。
…だから難攻不落だったとも言えるが」
findings.todokanai: "Well, Setsuna-chan, you've been ill informed on this stuff for a long time. So I guess you could say it's not your fault."

findings.highlight: "But Nagisa got into a vocational school here, right? I wonder if she broke up with Hayasaka… At that time, did he say anything?"
findings.evidenceJa:
「でも渚ってこっちの短大進んだよね？
早坂とは切れちゃったのかなぁ…
その辺りのこと、なんか言ってた？」
findings.explanation: Tomo attends a junior college; the English calls it a vocational school.
findings.japanese:
「でも渚ってこっちの短大進んだよね？
早坂とは切れちゃったのかなぁ…
その辺りのこと、なんか言ってた？」
findings.todokanai: "But Nagisa got into a vocational school here, right? I wonder if she broke up with Hayasaka… At that time, did he say anything?"

findings.highlight: We talk excitedly about our relatives in a way no other group can imitate
findings.evidenceJa: 六年間も同じ場所で過ごした俺たちだからこそ、誰にも真似できない、身内の話で盛り上がる。
findings.explanation: 身内の話 here means in-group or insider talk available to friends who shared the same place for six years. The English makes them talk about their relatives, severing the sentence from the group's shared school history.
findings.japanese:
六年間も同じ場所で過ごした俺たちだからこそ、
誰にも真似できない、身内の話で盛り上がる。
findings.todokanai: We talk excitedly about our relatives in a way no other group can imitate, for the four of us have spent the past six years living in the same place.

findings.highlight: While I understand that they're drunk
findings.evidenceJa: 酒とつまみが心許ないからと言って、二人が外に買い出しに出かけてから３０分以上…
findings.explanation: Io and Takeya went shopping because their alcohol and snack supplies looked inadequate. The English reads 酒 as their being drunk, drops the snacks, and no longer explains why they went out.
findings.japanese:
酒とつまみが心許ないからと言って、
二人が外に買い出しに出かけてから３０分以上…
findings.todokanai: While I understand that they're drunk, it's been over 30 minutes since they went out to do some shopping…

findings.highlight: Or perhaps this is something they've set up…
findings.evidenceJa:
しかもそれは、
果たしてあいつらのことなんだろうかというのか…
findings.explanation: Haruki asks whether the issue concerns Io and Takeya or himself and Setsuna; the English recasts it as something the friends arranged.
findings.japanese:
しかもそれは、
果たしてあいつらのことなんだろうかというのか…
findings.todokanai: Or perhaps this is something they've set up…

findings.highlight: one that's well-deserved for the two of them
findings.evidenceJa: あいつらに付け込まれるにふさわしい、とてつもない優しさに満ちていた。
findings.explanation: Setsuna's words are so extraordinarily kind that they are ripe for Io and Takeya to take advantage of. The English says the two friends deserve the kindness, reversing the exploitative dynamic Setsuna is forgiving.
findings.japanese:
あいつらに付け込まれるにふさわしい、
とてつもない優しさに満ちていた。
findings.todokanai: …Her words were filled with an unbelievable kindness, one that's well-deserved for the two of them.

findings.highlight: they just couldn't keep it to themselves anymore
findings.evidenceJa: けど、あそこまで“親友”になっちゃったから、もう引っ込みがつかなくなってるだけなんだ
findings.explanation: Takeya says Io has gone so far into the role of Setsuna's 'best friend' that she can no longer back out or change course. The English invents an inability to keep something secret, losing the explanation of why Io remains trapped in the relationship.
findings.japanese:
「けど、あそこまで“親友”になっちゃったから、
もう引っ込みがつかなくなってるだけなんだ」
findings.todokanai: "But they've come this far as 'good friends,' so maybe they just couldn't keep it to themselves anymore."

findings.highlight: No one made Setsuna-chan leave Haruki back thenーshe did it of her own volition.
findings.evidenceJa: 「あの時の春希から離れていかなかったのは、誰でもない、雪菜ちゃんの意志だったんだ」
findings.explanation: Takeya insists that it was Setsuna's own choice not to leave Haruki after the original crisis. The English says leaving him was her choice, reversing the defining decision on which his defense of her rests.
findings.japanese:
「あの時の春希から離れていかなかったのは、
誰でもない、雪菜ちゃんの意志だったんだ」
findings.todokanai: "No one made Setsuna-chan leave Haruki back thenーshe did it of her own volition."

findings.highlight: I was relieved by something
findings.evidenceJa: それでも彼女が、その瞬間何に安心したのか、それだけは、はっきり理解できたと思ってる。
findings.explanation: Haruki believes he understood exactly what Setsuna felt relieved about at that moment. The English makes Haruki himself the person who was relieved, reversing the emotional subject of his observation.
findings.japanese:
それでも彼女が、その瞬間何に安心したのか、
それだけは、はっきり理解できたと思ってる。
findings.todokanai: Even so, at that moment, the only thing that I think I clearly understood was that I was relieved by something.

findings.highlight: I'm making sure that I'm currently the same person
findings.evidenceJa: 今日の俺は、数日前の、パーティの時の俺と同じだって、そう、見極めたんだ。
findings.explanation: The continuing subject is Setsuna: she has assessed that today's Haruki is the same gentle Haruki she saw at the party. The English makes Haruki verify his own identity, erasing Setsuna's cautious test and the basis of her renewed approach.
findings.japanese:
今日の俺は、
数日前の、パーティの時の俺と同じだって、
そう、見極めたんだ。
findings.todokanai: I'm making sure that I'm currently the same person who attended Setsuna's birthday party just a few days ago.

findings.highlight: the number of courses we're taking haven't gone down at all
findings.evidenceJa: 「受ける講義も全然重ならなくなったし、顔合わせてる時間、だいぶ減っただろ？」
findings.explanation: Haruki says their classes no longer overlap at all, so they see much less of each other. The English says the number of courses has not decreased, confusing overlap with quantity and breaking the stated causal connection.
findings.japanese:
「受ける講義も全然重ならなくなったし、
顔合わせてる時間、だいぶ減っただろ？」
findings.todokanai: "Well, the number of courses we're taking haven't gone down at all, so the amount of time we've had to see each other has also lessened quite a lot, huh?"

findings.highlight: Only for today, the preparations for my move are all done.
findings.evidenceJa: 『今日までで、赴任の準備は全部終わった。あとは明日１３時発の飛行機で飛んでいくだけだ』
findings.explanation: Mari says all preparations for her posting were completed by today and that only tomorrow's 1 p.m. flight remains. The English's 'only for today' is not the temporal construction and obscures the countdown established by the message.
findings.japanese:
『今日までで、赴任の準備は全部終わった。
あとは明日１３時発の飛行機で飛んでいくだけだ』
findings.todokanai: "Only for today, the preparations for my move are all done. All that's left is to get on my flight at 1 PM."

findings.highlight: the kind of person to not follow each and every one of my instructions
findings.evidenceJa: 「お前は、いちいち細かく指示しないと動けないような奴じゃないよな？…そんなふうに育てた覚えはないからな？」
findings.explanation: Mari says Haruki is not the sort who cannot act unless every small detail is spelled out; she raised him to use initiative. The English asks whether he is the sort who fails to follow all her instructions, converting autonomy into obedience.
findings.japanese:
「お前は、いちいち細かく指示しないと
動けないような奴じゃないよな？
…そんなふうに育てた覚えはないからな？」
findings.todokanai: "You're not… the kind of person to not follow each and every one of my instructions, right? …At least, I don't remember training you that way."

findings.highlight: even though it must be unbearable to her, I keep on repeating the same mistakes
findings.evidenceJa: 何度も過ちを犯し、そのたびに何度も許され、そのことに耐えられず、また過ちを繰り返す。
findings.explanation: Haruki repeatedly sins, is repeatedly forgiven, cannot bear having been forgiven, and therefore sins again. The English assigns the unbearable burden to Setsuna, losing Haruki's self-destructive response to grace and the mechanism of the three-year cycle.
findings.japanese:
何度も過ちを犯し、そのたびに何度も許され、
そのことに耐えられず、また過ちを繰り返す。
findings.todokanai: No matter how many mistakes I've made, she's forgiven me at every turn; and even though it must be unbearable to her, I keep on repeating the same mistakes.

findings.highlight: Of course I loved you… I've always loved you all this time…
findings.evidenceJa: 「好きだよ…ずっと、好きなままだよ…っ」
findings.explanation: Haruki answers in the present: he loves Setsuna and has remained in love with her. The English changes both clauses to past love, erasing the deliberately cruel paradox that he still loves her while choosing someone else.
findings.japanese:
「好きだよ…
ずっと、好きなままだよ…っ」
findings.todokanai: "Of course I loved you… I've always loved you all this time…"

findings.highlight: We willingly shift our tightly intertwined hands away from each other.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちが繋げていた手を、自分から引きちぎってみせる。
findings.explanation: Setsuna herself tears apart the hands that joined them, demonstrating the strength required to complete the breakup for Haruki's sake. The English makes the separation mutual and gentle, erasing her singular agency and the violence of the image.
findings.japanese:
俺たちが繋げていた手を、
自分から引きちぎってみせる。
findings.todokanai: We willingly shift our tightly intertwined hands away from each other.

findings.highlight: Why is she leaving her apartment open like that!?
findings.evidenceJa: 「…３月には戻ってくるって言ったじゃない！なんで家を空けてるのよ！？」
findings.explanation: Sawako reminds Haruki that she told him Mari would return in March and demands to know why Haruki is away from home now. The English instead asks why Mari has left her apartment open, reversing the person whose absence created the crisis.
findings.japanese:
「…３月には戻ってくるって言ったじゃない！
なんで家を空けてるのよ！？」
findings.todokanai: "…Didn't she say she would come back in March!? Why is she leaving her apartment open like that!?"

findings.highlight: I hurried out of my lodging and headed for the station. I tried many times to find places with cell coverage, but I could only find the sounds of announcements coming from machines.
findings.evidenceJa:
ペンションを飛び出して駅に向かう道すがら、
電波の届くところを見つけては何度もかけたけど、
ずっと機械的なアナウンスが流れるだけだった。
findings.explanation: Haruki repeatedly called whenever he found cellular coverage and heard only an automated announcement; the English says he tried to find coverage but could find only announcements.
findings.japanese:
ペンションを飛び出して駅に向かう道すがら、
電波の届くところを見つけては何度もかけたけど、
ずっと機械的なアナウンスが流れるだけだった。
findings.todokanai: I hurried out of my lodging and headed for the station. I tried many times to find places with cell coverage, but I could only find the sounds of announcements coming from machines.

findings.highlight: I can reach Narita Airport in twelve hours
findings.evidenceJa: 「二回乗り継げば中央線に出られます。さっきネットで調べたんですけど、１２時過ぎには成田に着けるみたいです」
findings.explanation: Haruki says the route should get him to Narita just after noon, leaving minutes before the 1 p.m. flight. The English turns 12 o'clock into a twelve-hour journey, destroying the route's explicit deadline arithmetic.
findings.japanese:
「二回乗り継げば中央線に出られます。
さっきネットで調べたんですけど、
１２時過ぎには成田に着けるみたいです」
findings.todokanai: "If I transfer two times, I can get onto the Chuo line. I can reach Narita Airport in twelve hours, though that's only what I deduced from looking it up on the internet earlier."

findings.highlight: For the first time in the year, at that. Almost all of the first trains in the capital have been delayed
findings.evidenceJa: 「それも今年一番の。都内の電車、ほとんどが始発から運転を見合わせてる地下鉄以外」
findings.explanation: Sawako says this is the heaviest snowfall of the year and that, except for the subway, almost all Tokyo trains have suspended operation since first service. The English calls it the year's first snowfall and downgrades wholesale suspension to delays of the first trains.
findings.japanese:
「それも今年一番の。
都内の電車、ほとんどが始発から運転を見合わせてる
地下鉄以外」
findings.todokanai: "For the first time in the year, at that. Almost all of the first trains in the capital have been delayed other than the subway."

findings.highlight: Even if you're being stubborn, I'll catch up to you.
findings.evidenceJa: 意地でも、あなたに追いつくって。
findings.explanation: Haruki vows that by sheer stubborn determination, come what may, he will catch Mari. The English attaches the stubbornness to Mari, turning his own resolve into a concession about her behavior.
findings.japanese: 意地でも、あなたに追いつくって。
findings.todokanai: Even if you're being stubborn, I'll catch up to you.
